name: Eagle Crest
label: Eagle Crest
about_prose: Eagle Crest sits on 1,700 acres of high desert six miles west of downtown Redmond on Cline Falls Highway, climbing the east slopes of Cline Buttes above the Deschutes River canyon at 3,622 feet of elevation. It is a designated destination resort under Oregon's land use program, one of eight in the state, the legal mechanism that let a resort and residential community get built on rural land outside any city's growth boundary. Redmond's airport, Roberts Field, is a short drive northeast. Bend's Old Mill District is a straight run down US-97 to the south. Neither is a walk. Groceries, a hardware store, a pharmacy, all of it means getting in a car.

The resort broke ground in 1985 as a gated community of homesites, condominiums, and townhouses on the east side of Cline Falls Highway. A second phase opened in 1996 on the west side, built around the Ridge golf course, which had been completed in 1993. A third phase followed northwest of Cline Butte, adding six more subdivisions. Ownership has changed hands more than once since. Jeld-Wen, the Klamath Falls window and door manufacturer, developed and ran the resort originally. Northview Hotel Group bought it in 2010 with financing from Oaktree Capital Management. KDG Capital, a Florida investment firm, bought it again in 2018 and turned day-to-day hotel operations over to Aimbridge Hospitality. The homeowners associations that govern individual streets are separate from whoever owns the hotel side, but the golf courses, the lodge, and the conference center answer to that owner, not to the neighbors, and that owner has changed three times in forty years.

Three 18-hole golf courses share the property. The Resort Course, a par-72 designed by Gene Mason, runs along the canyon rim above the Deschutes River. The Ridge Course, also par 72, was laid out by John Thronson through native juniper and has hosted the Oregon Open. The Challenge Course is a shorter par-63 executive layout built for a quicker round. Three sports centers, named Resort, Ridge, and Lakeside, split the pools, tennis and pickleball courts, and fitness rooms across the different residential areas, and a day spa operates out of the Ridge center. More than 11 miles of paved paths connect the neighborhoods, plus a 1.5-mile trail that follows the Deschutes River. The Lodge at Eagle Crest holds 100 hotel rooms and 80 condominium units next to a 10,000-square-foot conference center, and Niblick and Greene's, the resort's full-service restaurant, runs alongside three smaller cafes.

Governance is split by geography, then split again by ownership type, and this is the part a buyer coming from a standard subdivision should understand going in. The Eagle Crest Master Association covers the east side of Cline Falls Highway and oversees several sub-associations underneath it, including the estate homesites, the villa estates, and the hotel condominiums. The west side, built around the Ridge course, answers to a separate HOA, the Ridge at Eagle Crest Homeowners Association, which represents more than 1,850 households on its own. A third association, the Vacation Resort Owners Association, holds 124 townhome units under deeded timeshare ownership, sold off in seasonal intervals. That structure means your neighbor on any given week could be a full-time resident, a guest in a nightly vacation rental, or a timeshare owner on their one week a year. Which HOA and which CC&Rs apply to a specific lot depends on which of the three development phases it was built in, and it is worth checking before you fall for a floor plan.

Eagle Crest falls inside the Redmond School District, which covers 550 square miles across Deschutes and Jefferson counties and also serves Alfalfa, Crooked River Ranch, Terrebonne, and Tumalo along with Redmond itself. The high school attendance boundary that includes Eagle Crest feeds Ridgeview High School, which opened in 2012 and also draws from Alfalfa and Tumalo. Outside the resort's own fence line, the Bureau of Land Management's Cline Buttes Recreation Area wraps both sides of the property, with a hiking and mountain bike trail network built largely through volunteer hours logged by the Redmond chapter of the Central Oregon Trail Alliance. Weigh Eagle Crest against a neighborhood inside the Bend or Redmond city limits and the trade is direct: more acreage, three golf courses, and open high desert sky, against a longer drive for everyday errands and an HOA structure that runs alongside an active resort, not around it.

amenities.name: Resort Course
amenities.description: Par-72 course playing 6,672 yards, designed by Gene Mason, following the Deschutes River canyon rim with holes perched above the river.

amenities.name: Ridge Course
amenities.description: Par-72 course playing 6,927 yards by John Thronson through native juniper forest. Host of the Oregon Open in 2006 and 2023.

amenities.name: Challenge Course
amenities.description: Par-63 executive course playing 4,160 yards, with four tee boxes per hole and a round of roughly three hours.

amenities.name: Resort Sports Center
amenities.description: Two indoor and two outdoor tennis courts, three racquetball courts, an outdoor pool, hot tub, sauna, fitness center, and game room.

amenities.name: Ridge Sports Center
amenities.description: Indoor lap pool, hot tub, wading pool, Cybex fitness center, basketball, pickleball, and volleyball courts.

amenities.name: Lakeside Sports Center
amenities.description: Outdoor infinity-edge pool, splash park, kiddie pool, outdoor basketball, four pickleball courts, and a fitness center.

amenities.name: Trails Network
amenities.description: Over 11 miles of paved paths plus a 1.5-mile Deschutes River trail, with access to river rafting and water sports.

amenities.name: The Spa at Eagle Crest
amenities.description: Day spa inside the Ridge Sports Center offering massage, facials, body treatments, and nail care using organic skincare lines.

amenities.name: Niblick and Greene's
amenities.description: Full-service restaurant at the resort with dinner service and live music, alongside the Aerie, Silverleaf, and Greenside cafes.

amenities.name: The Lodge and Conference Center
amenities.description: 100-room hotel with 80 condominium units and 10,000 square feet of meeting space, including a ballroom seating up to 360.

drive_times.note: Roberts Field, about 7.8 miles by road

course_specs.summary: Three 18-hole courses: Resort (par 72, 6,672 yds, Gene Mason), Ridge (par 72, 6,927 yds, John Thronson, host of the Oregon Open), and Challenge (par 63, 4,160 yds). An 18-hole live-turf putting course is also on site.
